markdown_report:
Propose bounded calibration of the temporal diagnostic adapter followed by one frozen predictive comparison. At 10% progress, this balances measurement reliability with testing recommendation quality; no validation improvement is established.

**Insights from the starting point.** First, recent-history deletion affected scores more than oldest-history deletion at an earlier checkpoint. Compaction also changes positions, preventing causal recency attribution. Second, unchanged-history repetition passed across all four datasets. Repeatability does not verify item alignment or intervention meaning. Third, the latest Industrial and Electronics negative-margin fractions were 24.61% and 27.97%. These in-sample observations motivate investigation, without establishing validation quality or useful thresholds.

**Insights from related work.** Metamorphic testing addresses missing recommendation oracles [1], while mutation analysis evaluates relation strength [4]. Constant or consistently misaligned scores can nevertheless pass permutation checks. Counterfactual faithfulness separates plausible explanations from prediction dependence [2]; neither establishes helpful dependence. Sampled-ranking research warns against extrapolating sampled comparisons to full-catalog quality [3]. Recency-sampling results motivate a predictive experiment [7], without establishing that diagnostic sensitivity predicts its benefit.

These insights define three directions: execution correctness, behavioral sensitivity, and predictive usefulness. The framework separates their evidence:

| Layer | Controlled relation | Supported conclusion |
|---|---|---|
| Scoring interface | Permutation plus independent known-score oracle | Exercised interface and mapping correctness |
| Earlier-history probe | Latest-item backend ignores earlier edits | Conditional probe specificity |
| History-independent control | Frequency backend ignores every edit | Control correctness |
| Host validation | Frozen baseline/intervention comparison | Conditional predictive evidence |

**Candidate ideas.** Scores denote originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive; negative assessment |
|---|---|---|
| Calibrate temporal probes with controlled backends [1,2,4] | 4/6/6 | Originality: useful integration; established techniques. Potential: reusable checks; accuracy link unproven. Difficulty: existing hooks help; independent routing and serialization oracles require care. |
| Add frequency-matched candidate stress tests [3] | 4/6/5 | Originality: useful combination; standard sampling. Potential: exposes candidate dependence; false negatives remain. Difficulty: training counts suffice; pool accounting expands scope. |
| Test a recency-weighted residual scorer [7] | 4/7/6 | Originality: diagnostic-motivated combination; established pooling. Potential: directly tests ranking gains; recency may reinforce shortcuts. Difficulty: small branch; predictor synchronization required. |

**Selected algorithm.** Retain compact calibration, then test one zero-initialized recency residual against unchanged SASRec. Freeze the training panel, independent mapping fixtures, individual mutations, predictive hypothesis, checkpoint rule, minimum useful gain, and computation cap before new validation feedback. Controls include candidate permutation, latest-item earlier-edit invariance, frequency all-edit invariance, batching, serialization, and route-specific known scores. Report residuals, coverage, mutation detection, and false alarms separately from trained-model sensitivity.

Preserve both diagnostic entry points, randomness isolation, model modes, all four routes, unavailable-data semantics, and twenty training-user full-catalog lists. Production inference remains the reference; unsupported masking controls stay unavailable. Update the predictor writer for the residual architecture. Select exclusively by pinned macro validation HR@10, report paired category effects, and permit no feedback-driven variants. This limits additional adaptation without correcting prior validation reuse [8].

idea.description: Retain a bounded calibration suite for the paired temporal diagnostic adapter, then conduct one preregistered predictive comparison between baseline SASRec and SASRec with a zero-initialized recency-weighted embedding residual. Use independent known-score and routing fixtures alongside metamorphic relations; distinguish interface correctness, control specificity, empirical sensitivity, and validation performance.
idea.motivation: The previous proposal correctly separated diagnostics from recommendation quality but overstated what permutation consistency establishes and deferred predictive testing. Constant scores and consistently incorrect item mappings can satisfy permutation equivariance. Meanwhile, supplied training-panel margins and temporal effects do not establish that sensitivity predicts useful interventions. At 10% progress, limited calibration followed by one simple predictive comparison offers a more direct use of the shared budget than expanding the diagnostic suite indefinitely. Qualitative feedback motivates specificity and recency hypotheses, while ownership, compatibility, satisfaction, and simulator traits remain unobserved.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve the original diagnostic contract: DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions. The actual-model branch must use view.model and architecture-compatible log2feats/predict_score. Never replace view.model with a diagnostic control or describe control outputs as trained-model predictions. Keep control scorers and predictive models explicitly separate.

Panel and reproducibility: Reuse an independently constructed persisted training-history panel without iterating the active loader. Cap calibration at 64 eligible users per category and three persisted perturbation draws, frozen before execution. Select users by a stable seed-42 digest of category and user ID, and persist exact prefixes, targets, unique candidate IDs, candidate permutations, edits, and eligibility. Retain final training targets and fixed diagnostic candidates across all conditions. These observations remain in-sample. Record category name explicitly rather than leaving dataset identifiers null; record checkpoint identity, category item-map fingerprint, adapter version, exact control definitions, panel fingerprint, counts, dtype, device, and runtime. If the existing panel has more users or draws, select and persist this deterministic subset without modifying the original panel.

Control definitions: Define the latest-item diagnostic backend as s(h,i)=dot(E[last_nonpadding(h)], E[i]), using detached trained item embeddings, no normalization or sequence features, and the category's actual embedding scale. Earlier-item substitutions and permutations must preserve the latest item and a nonempty history; latest-item deletion is outside this invariant. Define the frequency backend as s(h,i)=log1p(c_i), with counts from public training interactions within the routed category. It must ignore history. Neither backend is a newly trained reference model or evidence of predictive usefulness. Exclude empty histories from latest-item checks and report them explicitly.

Permutation and numerical checks: For every backend, persist a candidate-column permutation, score the permuted candidates, invert the permutation, and compare every per-candidate score by item identity. Use unique candidates in the panel; if an interface accepts repeated candidates, preserve their column identity in separate fixtures. Use float32 audit comparisons with atol=1e-5 and rtol=1e-4. Report maximum absolute residual, maximum scaled residual abs(a-b)/(atol+rtol*abs(reference)), nonfinite counts, attempted checks, and failures. Invariance applies only when its premises hold. The actual trained model is allowed to show zero sensitivity. Rank with descending score and a fixed internal-ID tie break for diagnostics, without changing the host evaluator's tie behavior.

Independent oracles: Retain the original synthetic distinct-score fixture and reversed-column injection, but label it as detection of one candidate-mapping fault rather than general calibration. Expand this into tiny, manually specified per-route fixtures with independently written external-ID-to-internal-row tables, distinct embedding rows, explicit expected raw scores, and hand-computed rankings. The oracle must not call the predictor's mapping helper or derive expected scores from its output. Include overlapping internal IDs with different route-specific expected scores so incorrect routing is exercised. Check a single example versus batched execution and compare before and after checkpoint serialization using trial-local temporary artifacts. Where the model interface supports it, jointly relabel histories, candidates, embedding rows, and mappings with padding ID 0 fixed; invert relabeling before comparison. Mark unsupported checks unavailable rather than claiming they passed. Synthetic fixtures test exercised pathways and cannot certify all real-data mappings.

Mutation evaluation: Inject one fault at a time into diagnostic copies or fixtures: constant outputs, ignored histories, candidate-position scores, sorted-but-unrestored outputs, off-by-one item lookup, swapped embedding rows, wrong dataset routing, and stale checkpoint mappings. Run every applicable relation against each mutant and its correct counterpart, reporting a relation-by-mutant matrix with detected, survived, equivalent, unexercised, or unsupported outcomes. Constant scores can survive permutation but should fail the distinct-score oracle. Consistently swapped rows may also survive permutation; the independent mapping oracle should expose exercised swaps. Ignored history requires a fixture with independently specified history-dependent expected scores, rather than an assumption that every trained model must change. Retain correct-control false-alarm counts and exact denominators; do not summarize heterogeneous mutants as a universal detection rate.

Production fidelity and temporal limitations: Before interpreting actual-model temporal probes, compare the adapter with the actual generated production predictor using the identical checkpoint, route, item mapping, left-padded histories, candidate IDs and order, device, dtype, and evaluation mode. Use a deterministic panel spanning short, long, and heavily padded histories. Compare raw per-candidate scores, nonfinite counts, maximum discrepancies, and diagnostic top-10 agreement under the declared tie rule. Report unavailable access to raw production scores explicitly; comparing the adapter with itself is not production verification. Failure invalidates the affected diagnostic interpretation, not automatically the checkpoint's host evaluation.

Do not silently add a key-padding mask to reproduce SASRec. The supplied source description uses absolute slot positions, causal attention, and final-slot readout; padding may still affect attention. Optional earlier-history controls require architecture-specific support: exclude selected history keys/values throughout every attention layer while keeping surviving positions and the final query; compact the identical survivors with explicit original position IDs; then use production-assigned compacted positions. These are distinct counterfactual branches, with potentially interacting effects. Verify unchanged-input fidelity against the corresponding reference branch, inspect intermediate tensors for nonfinite values, and label mask-corrected inference separately whenever it changes production computation. Zeroing item IDs alone is insufficient. Keep unsupported controls null with reasons; do not retrain solely to enable them during this bounded experiment.

State isolation: Preserve heterogeneous module modes, global Python/NumPy/Torch CPU/CUDA RNG states, accessible explicit-generator states, and registered buffers in try/finally. Restore and report unexpected buffer mutations. Controls must use detached copies and must never mutate the trained checkpoint. Active training workers and samplers are not touched. Do not claim subsequent optimizer-step equivalence unless measured independently. Aggregate actual-model draw effects within users, then within categories; macro means require all four categories. Report invariant failures per category instead of hiding them in a macro average. Timing and omitted checks remain visible.

One predictive comparison: Before observing new validation results, freeze exactly two configurations: unchanged RecHarness sasrec_perdataset and the same model with a scalar recency residual. At every position t, define a causal pooled embedding p_t=sum_{j<=t,seq_j!=0} 2^(-(t-j)/10) E[seq_j] divided by the corresponding weight sum. Compute h'_t=h_t+alpha*p_t, with one unconstrained scalar alpha per dataset initialized to zero. Keep the baseline's output scoring and loss unchanged. Pool only preceding/current input tokens, never shifted positive labels or future positions; use positions as ages, without claiming elapsed-time modeling. Set the pooled vector to zero for an empty prefix. Initialize common parameters identically at seed 42; construct alpha with zeros without consuming random draws. Record learned alpha values and branch norms as descriptive diagnostics, not explanations or selection targets.

Freeze the hypothesis that this residual improves macro validation HR@10 through a simple additional recency pathway; do not assert that larger baseline sensitivity predicts larger benefit. Fix a practical threshold of an absolute 0.005 macro-HR@10 gain before the comparison. This is a decision threshold, not a claim of statistical significance. Use the same baseline optimizer, learning rate, loss, negative sampler, batch size, model width, maximum sequence length, and unchanged preprocessing. Respect SASREC_EPOCHS, defaulting to 200, and evaluate the final scheduled checkpoint only; do not select intermediate checkpoints or retune by category after feedback. Fit each configuration sequentially on one GPU and evaluate each once with the unchanged host validation protocol. Retain both predictor artifacts and the complete comparison even if the intervention loses. Benchmark selection still follows measured host macro HR@10; report the practical threshold separately.

Budget: Predeclare at most 120 GPU-seconds total for the compact calibration across four categories and at most 8,000 GPU-seconds for the complete predictive comparison, subject to a smaller host-reported remaining allowance. Reserve these amounts before execution using the host's existing budget accounting; all diagnostics, training, debugging, and failed trials count. If the remaining budget cannot cover the declared experiment, report it unexecuted rather than starting an open-ended pilot. If the cap interrupts fitting, report the comparison incomplete and do not substitute a favorable intermediate checkpoint. Do not introduce validation-driven variants after the comparison. Record all queries and checkpoint rules. These limits reduce additional adaptive exposure but cannot remove previous validation reuse or establish general calibration of diagnostic usefulness.

Evaluation: Preserve the host's 200 validation users per category, 99 unique negatives, evaluation seed 42, and equal-weight macro HR@10. Report both category effects and the macro difference. If the host exposes paired per-user hit indicators, compute intervention-minus-baseline differences and 1,000 seed-42 paired-user bootstrap replicates stratified by category, resampling users within each category and averaging category means equally. These intervals condition on the fitted models, validation sample, and candidates; they exclude training-seed variation and adaptive search bias. If paired records are unavailable, report that limitation without reconstructing or replacing host evaluation. One comparison supplies predictive evidence for this intervention, not evidence that sensitivity identifies which interventions will work.

Inference integration: Change log2feats to return the residual-augmented per-position features and keep predict_score consistent with that representation. The predictor writer and working/predict.py must instantiate the same architecture, restore alpha and all original parameters, preserve category routing and item maps, and apply identical causal pooling. Store an architecture/version flag and residual configuration with checkpoints. Run serialization and production-score fidelity checks on this architecture. Baseline checkpoints retain their original architecture flag and scoring path. Do not leave the predictor writer on the baseline model while training the residual.

Native recommendation requirement: Retain five real training users per category, twenty total, selected reproducibly before inspecting recommendations. Each receives full-catalog, training-unseen recommendations through the actual trained scorer, with chunked catalog scoring. Preserve original unseen eligibility across perturbations. Keep these qualitative lists separate from calibration fixtures, sampled training-panel metrics, and validation selection. Neither title similarity nor a residual coefficient establishes ownership, compatibility, current intent, satisfaction, or a causal explanation.

Task restrictions: Use only public interaction histories, titles, descriptions, and available timestamps. Ratings, reviews, item categories, prices, stores, and simulator diversity/conformity traits are unavailable and unused. Keep DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes, single-GPU execution, unchanged official splits and host evaluator, and trial-local artifacts. Fetch no external datasets or pretrained weights. No training or validation gains are claimed before measurement.
idea.pseudocode:
class DiagnosisProbe:
    def __init__(self, view, device):
        self.view, self.device = view, device

    def run_full_diagnosis(self, train_loader):
        # Compatibility argument retained; never consume the active loader.
        panel = load_fixed_training_panel(max_users=64, draws=3, seed=42)
        state = capture_modes_rng_and_buffers(self.view.model)
        try:
            self.view.model.eval()
            with torch.no_grad():
                trained = ActualModelBackend(self.view)
                latest = LastItemDotBackend(detached_copy(self.view.item_emb))
                frequency = TrainingFrequencyBackend(self.view.user_train)

                record_independent_route_specific_known_score_oracles()
                record_single_fault_relation_matrix()
                record_batching_serialization_and_supported_relabeling_checks()
                record_adapter_vs_actual_production_predictor_fidelity()

                for batch in panel:
                    for backend in (trained, latest, frequency):
                        original = backend.score(batch.prefix, batch.candidates)
                        permuted = backend.score(
                            batch.prefix, batch.permuted_candidates)
                        record_per_item_equivariance(
                            original, invert_candidate_permutation(permuted),
                            atol=1e-5, rtol=1e-4)

                    for variant in batch.persisted_variants:
                        record_actual_model_effect(trained, batch, variant)
                        if variant.preserves_latest_item_and_nonempty_history:
                            require_score_invariance(latest, batch, variant)
                        require_score_invariance(frequency, batch, variant)

                record_original_distinct_score_reversal_fixture()
                record_five_training_users_full_catalog_lists(trained)
                return {
                    'metrics': summarize_counts_residuals_mutants_and_runtime(),
                    'metric_definitions': formulas_premises_scope_and_limits()
                }
        finally:
            restore_and_check_state(self.view.model, state)


# Executed separately from DiagnosisProbe; frozen before new validation feedback.
freeze_experiment(
    configurations=['baseline', 'baseline_plus_recency_residual'],
    half_life_positions=10,
    alpha_initial_value=0,
    checkpoint_rule='final scheduled epoch only',
    minimum_useful_absolute_macro_gain=0.005,
    calibration_gpu_seconds=120,
    comparison_gpu_seconds=8000,
    validation_driven_variants=0)


def residual_features(sequence, baseline_features, item_embeddings, alpha):
    # All inputs at position t precede its next-item training label.
    weights = causal_nonpadding_weights(sequence, half_life_positions=10)
    pooled = weighted_prefix_mean(item_embeddings(sequence), weights)
    return baseline_features + alpha * pooled


for configuration in frozen_configurations:
    initialize_common_parameters_identically(seed=42)
    model = build_frozen_configuration(configuration)
    train_with_unchanged_baseline_protocol_and_budget(model)
    if training_completed:
        write_architecture_matched_checkpoint_and_predictor(model)
        verify_serialized_production_scores(model)
        request_one_unchanged_host_validation_evaluation()
    else:
        record_incomplete_comparison_without_checkpoint_substitution()

report_category_and_macro_differences()
report_paired_user_intervals_only_if_host_records_available()
# No feedback-driven variants; no test access or evaluator replacement.


def diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return render_grounded_prompt(
        metrics=raw_diagnosis['metrics'],
        definitions=raw_diagnosis['metric_definitions'],
        distinguish_controls_from_trained_predictions=True,
        distinguish_consistency_from_semantic_alignment=True,
        distinguish_invariant_failure_from_empirical_sensitivity=True,
        distinguish_predictive_comparison_from_probe_calibration=True,
        forbid_unsupported_accuracy_causality_and_trait_claims=True)

# Pseudocode: helpers require integration with the actual architecture,
# predictor writer, routing contract, and host budget/evaluation interfaces.

originality.positive: Connects independent mapping oracles, controlled diagnostic backends, mutation checks, and a frozen recency intervention in the required evaluation workflow.
originality.negative: Metamorphic testing, mutation analysis, recency pooling, and residual connections are established; their integration is incremental rather than a new model principle.

future_potential.positive: Produces reusable interface checks and a direct, bounded test of a simple predictive intervention across all four datasets.
future_potential.negative: A single fixed-seed comparison cannot establish broad generalization or show that temporal sensitivity predicts intervention benefits; recency may amplify popularity or short-term shortcuts.

code_difficulty.positive: The residual adds one scalar and a causal pooling operation while retaining the baseline objective and existing diagnostic hooks.
code_difficulty.negative: Independent route oracles, production fidelity, mutation accounting, budget enforcement, and synchronized checkpoint/predictor changes require substantially more integration than the previous difficulty score of four implied.

related_work.title: [1] An empirical study on metamorphic testing for recommender systems
contributions: Studies recommender reliability through relations between executions when exact expected recommendations are unavailable.
Motivates explicit invariance checks and controlled error injections.
limitations: Does not establish the proposed temporal fault-signature suite for SASRec.
Passing metamorphic checks does not demonstrate recommendation accuracy or semantic item alignment.

related_work.title: [2] Walk the Talk? LLM faithfulness
contributions: Uses counterfactual interventions to examine whether cited explanatory concepts influence predictions.
Motivates separating textual plausibility from measured model dependence.
limitations: Does not directly validate the proposed SASRec controls or residual scorer.
Prediction sensitivity alone establishes neither causal user preferences nor useful predictive dependence.

related_work.title: [3] On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can misrepresent full-catalog comparisons.
Supports keeping sampled training-panel diagnostics distinct from benchmark selection.
limitations: Does not prescribe the calibration suite or predictive intervention.
Its sampling critique does not authorize changing the task's pinned evaluator.

related_work.title: [4] Mutation-based evaluation of metamorphic relations
contributions: Provides precedent for evaluating metamorphic relations through controlled program mutations.
Motivates reporting which individual faults each relation detects.
limitations: The supplied search summary does not establish recommender-specific coverage for the proposed mutations.
Detection depends on exercised fixtures; surviving, equivalent, and unexercised mutants require separate interpretation.

related_work.title: [5] SASRec.pytorch implementation
contributions: Illustrates SASRec inference with absolute slot embeddings, causal attention, final-slot features, and candidate embedding scores.
Motivates checking padding and positional behavior against the actual production implementation.
limitations: A mutable external implementation is not proof of the pinned RecHarness model's exact behavior.
Adding masking or explicit position controls can change checkpoint computation.

related_work.title: [6] PyTorch MultiheadAttention documentation
contributions: Documents attention masks and key-padding masks as distinct mechanisms.
Supports architecture-specific handling of padding visibility and mask semantics.
limitations: Documentation alone cannot establish production-score equivalence.
Fully blocked query rows and implementation-specific behavior require measured finite-value checks.

related_work.title: [7] Recency-sampling experiments for sequential recommendation
contributions: The supplied search summary reports accuracy and training-efficiency benefits from recency sampling across sequential architectures, including SASRec.
Motivates a bounded experiment involving recency.
limitations: Recency sampling differs from the proposed embedding residual.
Does not establish gains on the four pinned categories or show that perturbation sensitivity forecasts improvement.

related_work.title: [8] Adaptive holdout research
contributions: Explains how repeated adaptive feedback can overfit validation data.
Motivates freezing configurations, checkpoint rules, query counts, and decision thresholds before new feedback.
limitations: A fixed comparison cannot erase earlier validation reuse.
The proposal does not implement a reusable-holdout mechanism or obtain its formal guarantees.
